ticket.found_by: measuring what a dry run left behind in the operator's own read-only home
ticket.model_change: None. The claim is about a filesystem side effect of acquiring a lock, and this model has neither a filesystem nor a lock.
ticket.objective: A dry run created `~/.skill-manager/.materialization/` and a zero-byte `.materialization/.home.lock` inside it. `--dry-run` is documented "Compute and print the whole report, write nothing". Content-benign, and still: it breaks the contract, it would fail outright against a read-only or frozen destination, and it is exactly the write a caller reaches for `--dry-run` to avoid. The lock was acquired BEFORE the plan was computed, so no amount of care later could have prevented it.
ticket.resolution: HomeLock.acquireWithoutCreating. The in-process ReentrantLock is taken unconditionally -- it is memory, not disk, and it excludes every writer in this JVM completely. The OS file lock is taken only when the lock file already EXISTS, and that is not a concession: creating that file is the first thing acquiring the lock does, so its absence is positive evidence that no process anywhere holds it. There is nothing to exclude against and nothing to wait for. Where the file is there, the ordinary path runs unchanged, wait included. The residual window -- a peer that begins AFTER the check -- is bounded and stated rather than waved away: every real writer stages each unit and swaps it in atomically, so no unit is ever read half-written, and the worst case is a report naming units from either side of a peer's pass, which is what it would have said had the peer run a millisecond earlier.
